label: prop:gravity-spectral-prefactor
title: Catalan's $G$ as the universal-residue prefactor of the unified mass formula
html:
Working over A = H_n(R, q), the universal curvature-rank tail \mathfrak{m}^{\geq 4}_{q,\mathcal{K}}(\mathcal{T}) of the unified mass formula (universal residue) carries a stratum-dependent prefactor:

  \alpha \;=\; m_e \cdot 8\,G,

where G = \sum_{k \geq 0} (-1)^k/(2k+1)^2 \approx 0.9159655942 is Catalan's constant, so that 8G = \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) \approx 7.3277 is the hyperbolic volume of the Borromean complement — two regular ideal octahedra of volume 4G each. The coefficient 8 is therefore fixed by the octahedral decomposition, not chosen. This is the same prefactor as binding scale from Catalan's constant.

The associated dimensionless spectral ratio at substrate parameter q is:

  G_q \;=\;
  \frac{\alpha(q)}{8\, m_e}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{8\, m_e}
  \cdot \lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{\mathfrak{m}^{\geq k}_{q,\mathcal{K}}(\mathcal{T})}
                                   {\sum_{j \geq k} \Phi_j(\mathcal{K}, \mathcal{T})}
  \,\in\, R,

the limiting ratio of the deep-tower mass to the Plancherel-weighted character residue.

Scope. G_q is a dimensionless spectral invariant of the curvature-rank tail. It carries no [\mathrm{length}]^3[\mathrm{mass}]^{-1}[\mathrm{time}]^{-2} content, and no derivation, dimensional bridge, or comparison against a measured gravitational coupling is offered here or elsewhere in this corpus. Whether it bears any relation to Newton's constant is open.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows operates on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs: real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. The generic categorical and q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring. Only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
